market_context: United States and general English-speaking market
title: Whole, 2% and skim milk: nutrition differences

seo.title: Whole vs. 2% vs. skim milk: nutrition compared
seo.meta_description: The biggest difference is fat and calories, not protein or calcium. Compare USDA values for whole, 2% and skim milk per 100 g and per cup.
seo.search_intent: Compare whole, reduced-fat and skim milk nutrition

excerpt: Removing milk fat mainly lowers calories, total fat and saturated fat. USDA references per 100 g: whole milk 61 calories and 3.25 g fat; 2% milk 50 calories and about 2 g fat; skim milk 34 calories and 0.08 g fat. Protein stays close to 3.2–3.4 g and calcium remains around 113–122 mg.
content_html:
Whole, reduced-fat and skim milk are more alike than their labels sometimes make them sound. Most of the nutritional change comes from removing milk fat.

USDA comparison per 100 g

Whole2%Skim
Calories615034
Fat3.25 g~2.0 g0.08 g
Protein3.15 g3.3 g3.37 g
Carbohydrate4.8 g4.8 g4.96 g
Calcium113 mg120 mg122 mg

Protein and calcium barely move. Fat and calories do.

What a cup looks like

Using typical cup weights, whole milk is about 149 calories per cup, 2% about 123, and skim roughly 83. All still provide around 8 g protein.

Skimming does not remove lactose

The carbohydrate stays near 5 g/100 g in all three because lactose is in the watery portion of milk, not the fat globules.

What about vitamins?

In the U.S., lower-fat milk is commonly fortified with vitamin A and vitamin D, while whole milk is generally vitamin D fortified. Label values therefore reflect both natural composition and fortification practices.

Which one should you choose?

Skim or low-fat milk reduces calories and saturated fat while keeping protein and calcium. Whole milk provides more fat and a richer texture. Personal needs, age and the rest of the diet matter more than treating one as universally superior.

faq.question: Does skim milk have less protein?
faq.answer: No. USDA values are very similar: about 3.37 g/100 g skim versus 3.15 g whole.

faq.question: Does skim milk have less calcium?
faq.answer: No. The USDA references are about 122 mg/100 g skim and 113 mg whole.

faq.question: How many fewer calories does skim have?
faq.answer: About 27 fewer per 100 g, or roughly 65 fewer in a typical cup compared with whole milk.

faq.question: Does removing fat remove lactose?
faq.answer: No. Carbohydrate remains close to 5 g/100 g in all three.
